# Anaesthetic depth, ventilatory drive and neuromuscular block

## Purpose

<!-- hand:purpose -->
> Draft — owner review pending.

The neuro model: anaesthetic depth (a BIS-like index and a separate consciousness level), depression of the drive to
breathe, neuromuscular block with the train-of-four picture a stimulator records, neostigmine reversal, and the set
point and pattern of spontaneous breathing. It has no pharmacokinetics of its own: it reads effect-site concentrations
and MAC fractions from the drug model and turns them into the lungs' drive inputs and the depth and TOF tiles. For a
clinician-educator it explains depth, apnoea and residual block; for an embedding developer it runs at 10 Hz after the
drug model and before the respiratory pipeline (`l2/neuro/pipeline.ts`).
<!-- /hand:purpose -->

## Equations in words

<!-- hand:equations -->
> Draft — owner review pending.

- Depth index: a hypnotic interaction term U sums each agent's effect-site concentration over its potency (propofol,
  potent volatile MAC plus N2O at weight 0.1, opioid at weight 0.2, midazolam); DI = 93·(1 − U^γ/(U^γ + 1)) with γ 1.89
  below U = 1 and 1.47 above (Eleveld BIS 2024; `tables §5d`; `l2/neuro/depth.ts`). It is not a BIS algorithm.
- MAC is age-adjusted, MAC40·10^(−0.00269·(age − 40)) (Mapleson; `l2/neuro/depth.ts`). Ketamine counts × 0.1 on the
  index but in full for consciousness, which is a separate level (Hirota & Lambert 2001; `l2/neuro/depth.ts`).
- Opioid ventilatory depression dOp = x^1.25/(1 + x^1.25), x = the remifentanil-equivalent concentration at the
  ventilatory site ÷ 0.92 ng/mL (Bouillon 2003); hypnotic depression uses propofol C50 1.17 µg/mL and volatile C50
  0.8 MAC [ENG, Nieuwenhuijs 2003] (`l2/neuro/drive.ts`).
- The opioid–hypnotic combination for breathing is per class: opioid plus benzodiazepine strongly synergistic (fit to
  Bailey 1990), opioid plus propofol or volatile additive [ENG]; apnoea when resting ventilation falls below 0.42 of
  normal, resuming above 0.5 (`l2/neuro/drive.ts`).
- Neuromuscular block B = Ce^γ/(Ce^γ + EC50^γ) and T1 = 1 − B; TOF count needs T1 above 3/10/20/25 %; TOF ratio = T1^2.5
  capped at 1 for non-depolarisers; succinylcholine shows no fade until phase II (3–7 mg/kg cumulative); post-tetanic
  count 1–15 as T1 rises from 1 to 3 % (`tables §5d`; `l2/neuro/nmb.ts`).
- Diaphragm and larynx need 1.73 × the thumb's EC50 (Plaud 1995; `l2/neuro/nmb.ts`), so breathing returns while the TOF
  is still low.
- Neostigmine multiplies the non-depolariser EC50 by 1 + 0.7·x/(x + 0.3), x = the drug model's acetylcholine gain − 1;
  the ceiling means a deep block cannot be reversed and the block returns if the drug fades first
  (`l2/neuro/neostigmine.ts`; `tables §5d`).
- Spontaneous breathing: the PaCO2 set point falls to Winter's 1.5·HCO3 + 8 in metabolic acidosis (Albert, Dell &
  Winters 1967) and rises 0.7 mmHg per mmol/L of excess HCO3 in alkalosis, capped at 55 mmHg (Javaheri & Kazemi 1987);
  ventilation is the lungs' chemoreflex × (1 − opioid depression) × (1 − hypnotic depression), and tidal volume scales
  with diaphragm strength (`l2/neuro/spont.ts`).
<!-- /hand:equations -->

### [`l2/neuro/neostigmine.ts`](../../packages/engine-core/src/l2/neuro/neostigmine.ts)

| Name | Value | Unit | Source / tag | Comment |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `NEO_SMAX` | `0.7` | — | tables §5d; brief §4.9; [P]; [TXT]; [ENG]; [ENG, fitted on the drug model's gain curve within 0.3–1.2: 0.05 mg/kg at TOF 2 → TOFR 0.9 in 18.3 min (band 8–20; 0.6 gave 22.0); 0.07 mg/kg at PTC → TOFR 0.35 at 10 min] | Neostigmine's NMB effect (tables §5d Neo row: ceiling [P], peak ~10 min [TXT]; brief §4.9). The drug, its time course and its muscarinic effects are the drug model's gamma row, which publishes an acetylcholine gain on the bus (`bus.nmb.achGain`, 1 = none). The neuro model turns the gain into a multiplier on the non-depolarisers' EC50: m = 1 + NEO_SMAX · x/(x + NEO_G50), x = achGain − 1 The CEILING is structural: m < 1 + NEO_SMAX however large the dose, so a deep block (TOF count < 2) cannot be lifted to recovery, and when the drug model's curve fades before spontaneous recovery is complete the block returns (recurarisation). NEO_SMAX 0.7 [ENG] IS the ceiling (never fitted). NEO_G50 0.3 [ENG, fitted on the drug model's gain curve within 0.3–1.2: 0.05 mg/kg at TOF 2 → TOFR 0.9 in 18.3 min (band 8–20; 0.6 gave 22.0); 0.07 mg/kg at PTC → TOFR 0.35 at 10 min]. |
| `NEO_G50` | `0.3` | — | — | — |

| `BRAINSTEM_CBF_MIN` | `0.2` | — | Med 1992; Circulation 2008; [P]; [ENG] | Brainstem-perfusion gate. After the circulation stops, agonal gasps persist for seconds to ≈ 2 min, then apnoea; after the circulation returns the drive comes back over minutes (Clark JJ et al., Ann Emerg Med 1992;21:1464–1467; Bobrow BJ et al., Circulation 2008;118:2550–2554) [P]. The gate closes when the organ model's CBF is below BRAINSTEM_CBF_MIN or there is no flow at all (pulseless / CO 0). CBF < 20 % of rest (the ruling's threshold) [ENG] |
| `GASP_ONSET_S` | `30` | s | [ENG, ruling] | unperfused for > 30 s → gasps only [ENG, ruling] |
| `GASP_END_S` | `120` | s | [ENG, ruling] | gasps fade to apnoea by 2 min [ENG, ruling] |
| `GASP_RR` | `6` | — | [ENG, ruling "RR ≤ 6"] | gasp rate ceiling (/min) [ENG, ruling "RR ≤ 6"] |
| `GASP_VT_FRAC` | `0.3` | — | [ENG] | gasp VT ceiling × the resting VT ("small VT") [ENG] |
| `GATE_REOPEN_S` | `120` | s | [ENG, ruling "1–3 min"] | the drive reopens linearly over 2 min once perfused [ENG, ruling "1–3 min"] |
| `CENTRAL_TAU_S` | `90` | s | Dahan et al. 1990; [TXT; τ 90 s ENG] | The CO2 stimulus is partly CENTRAL (brain ECF PCO2, τ ≈ 60–150 s) and partly peripheral (carotid, fast): Dahan et al. 1990 J Physiol 423:615 (dynamic end-tidal forcing: central τ ≈ 100 s, peripheral share ≈ 0.3) [TXT; τ 90 s ENG]. The drive reads 0.3·PaCO2 + 0.7·Pc. At steady state Pc = PaCO2 (no change to any resting value). |
| `PERIPH_SHARE` | `0.3` | — | — | — |
| `VT_MAX_ML_KG` | `35` | mL/kg | Hey et al. 1966; [ENG size] | The tidal-volume ceiling of the chemical drive — VT plateaus at 50–60 % of the vital capacity (Hey et al. 1966 Respir Physiol 1:193), VC ≈ 60–70 mL/kg IBW → 35 mL/kg IBW, × fatigue (weakness stays nmbVtMult's) [ENG size]. |
| `VT_REST_ML_KG` | `7` | mL/kg | [TXT: the lung-protective range gas/params.ts already quotes] | A resting tidal volume per kg IBW, the size the weak diaphragm's cap reaches at DIAPH_EFFECTIVE (6–8 mL/kg [TXT: the lung-protective range gas/params.ts already quotes]). |
| `ALK_SLOPE` | `0.7` | — | Dis 1987; Narins & Emmett 1980; tables §5b.1 | Metabolic alkalosis is compensated by hypoventilation — PaCO2 rises 0.7 mmHg per mmol/L HCO3 above normal (Javaheri S, Kazemi H. Am Rev Respir Dis 1987;136:1011; Narins & Emmett 1980 "Boston rules"), rarely beyond 55 mmHg (the hypoxaemic drive limits it). The reference is the blood model's normal HCO3 plus the chronic renal compensation the patient's own resting PaCO2 implies (the blood model's CHRONIC_HCO3_PER_MMHG, tables §5b.1), plus a 0.1 mmol/L deadband, so a compensated chronic hypercapnic profile is not read as a metabolic alkalosis and a resting patient is exactly unchanged. |
| `ALK_PACO2_MAX` | `55` | — | — | — |

| `ACUTE_HCO3_PER_MMHG` | `0.1` | mmHg | Cohen & Schwartz 1965 | Acute CO2 buffering, mmol/L HCO3 per mmHg PaCO2 (Brackett, Cohen & Schwartz 1965 NEJM 272:6; the blood model's own 0.11–0.15). |
